data.summary: This directory is a single scenario definition for the `fzf` command-line fuzzy finder within a scenario-based tool provisioning system (aio-config). It pairs declarative metadata (`scenario.toml`, consumed by `aio-config gen`) with the executable install fragment (`fragment.Dockerfile`) that installs fzf via `mise use -g` and verifies the binary is resolvable in both login and non-login shells. It contains no application business logic — it is pure infrastructure/configuration for image building.

file_insights.name: fragment.Dockerfile
file_insights.summary: Dockerfile fragment that installs the pinned fzf version with `mise use -g` and asserts the `fzf` binary is available in both login and non-login shells.
file_insights.source_summary: Declares `ARG FZF_VERSION={{version}}` and runs `mise use -g "fzf@${FZF_VERSION}"`, then lists the installed tool with `mise ls fzf` and fails the build with an explicit MISSING message if `command -v fzf` fails under a login shell or a non-login shell. Comments note that the binary name is the canonical `fzf` (no Debian-style renaming to batcat/fdfind equivalents).
file_insights.detailed_description: This fragment represents the L2 shell layer of the image build, responsible for provisioning the fzf fuzzy finder. It relies on `mise use -g` being a read-modify-write, idempotent operation so that the fragment can be composed with other mise tool fragments in any Docker layer order without an aggregation step. It ends with verification checks using `bash -lc` and `bash -c` to ensure the binary resolves in both login and non-login shell contexts.
responsibilities: Declare a versioned build argument for the fzf release
Install fzf globally through the mise aqua backend
Verify installation via `mise ls fzf` output
Fail fast if fzf is not on PATH in login or non-login shells

file_insights.name: scenario.toml
file_insights.summary: Declarative scenario metadata describing the fzf installation scenario, including its id, category, installer backend, and the pinned 0.74.4 version.
file_insights.source_summary: Contains the fields `id = "fzf"`, `name = "fzf"`, a Chinese description describing fzf as a command-line fuzzy finder (completion/history search/file selection) installed via the mise aqua backend into /opt/mise/installs, `category = "shell"`, `installer = "mise"`, and one `[[versions]]` table with label and version both set to `0.74.4`.
file_insights.detailed_description: This TOML file is the machine-readable descriptor consumed by `aio-config gen` for fragment resolution; it tells the generator what scenario exists and where its install steps live. It identifies the scenario as belonging to the `shell` category and using the `mise` installer, with fzf installed under /opt/mise/installs via the mise aqua backend. It exposes a single pinned version entry (label and version 0.74.4) that parameterizes the `{{version}}` placeholder in the adjacent Dockerfile fragment.
responsibilities: Identify the scenario by id and display name
Categorize the tool as a shell-layer scenario
Declare mise as the installer backend
Pin the exact tool version (0.74.4) used for fragment templating
